newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Aug jobs data revised to show stronger rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Aug jobs data revised to show stronger rise.

text.p: The Labor Department said Friday August non-farm payrolls had risen by 257,000 after it revised data to reflect corrected seasonal adjustment factors.
On Oct 4, the department had reported August payrolls rose by a revised 241,000, down from a previously-reported 250,000.
The corrected data also showed total private average weekly hours rose by 0.2 percent, instead of an earlier reported 0.3 percent increase.
Average hourly earnings for the same group rose $0.06 in the corrected data instead of by the previously reported $0.05.
The department said the error correction had "only a negligible effect on employment, hours and earnings estimates."

The correction had no effect on July total non-farm payrolls. In June, non-farm payroll jobs rose 205,000 instead of the earlier reported 219,000. May non-farm jobs rose 410,000 compared to the 407,000 jobs reported earlier.
In April non-farm payrolls rose 172,000 instead of 191,000, while March payrolls were up 171,000, compared with 158,000 reported earlier.
Total average weekly hours data for March through July 1996 were unaffected by the corrections.
June hourly earnings rose by $0.09 instead of $0.10, while May was revised to $0.02 compared to an earlier reported $0.01. July, April and March data were not affected by the changes.
Corrections to the seasonal factors were made after a minor coding error in the program used to create seasonal factors was uncovered and corrected, the department said.
